sections.heading: How to Play Devourer
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Devourer"][color=c12]Devourer Demon Hunter Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]

Devourer Demon Hunter uses two separate resources and features a different cadence to their rotation depending on whether you are inside [spell=1217607] or not. This can seem overwhelming at first, but the spec has some core concepts to help follow and keep things on track. The core concepts to keep in mind in single target are these, in order of importance:


[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_12_dh_void_ability_soulfragments size=medium type=round color=c12 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c12]Avoid Resource Waste:[/color][/b] Use [spell=1217607] and [spell=473728] as soon as they are available. To take full advantage of our tier set, look to use [spell=1226019] whenever it will collect 4 or more souls.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_112_ability_demonhunter_metamorphasisvoid size=medium type=round color=c12 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c12]Plan Cooldown Usage:[/color][/b] The goals of your [spell=1217607] windows will depend on your chosen hero talent tree. [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] looks to use all the melee abilities, and to cycle through as many Void Metamorphosis windows as possible, while [symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color] looks to extend one window, casting as many [spell=1221167] as possible. Either way, a lot of your damage comes from these windows, so ensure minimal disruption from them.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_12_dh_void_ability_reap size=medium type=round color=c12 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c12]Accelerate Your Rotation:[/color][/b] [spell=1226019] is used to accelerate into [spell=473728] and [spell=1217607], collecting souls, generating Fury and dealing a large amount of your damage. In season 2, both hero talent trees are looking to cast it as much as possible in Single Target, using it whenever it will collect 4+ souls (10 for [spell=1239524]), to take advantage of our tier set.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=Classicon_demonhunter_void_64 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c12][/icon] Best Devourer Demon Hunter Rotation[/h2]
For all forms of content, Devourer follows a priority list of what spells to cast. It looks to manage its dual resource system to get into [spell=1217607] as soon as possible. 

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Devourer Demon Hunter: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.


[wrapper width=70%][center][box border=true]
	[center][large][b][color=white]Hero Talent Master Switches[/color][/b][/large]
	[pad]
	You can use the master switches below to flip the [b][i]entire page's[/i][/b] options to your selected choice.[/center]

	[center]
	[wrapper width=95%]
		[grid column-width=49%]
			[display-option="void-scarred" radio="Hero" icon=inv_12_voiddh_ability_demonsurge checked]Void-Scarred[/display-option]
			[display-option="annihilator" radio="Hero" icon=inv_12_dh_void_ability_voidfall]Annihilator[/display-option]
		[/grid]
	[/wrapper]
	[/center]
[/box][/center][/wrapper]
[br]
[tabs name="Rotations" uniform=true]

[tab name="Single-Target Priority" icon=spell_holy_divinespirit]
	[h3 toc="Single Target Priority" type=bar][color=c12] Best Devourer Demon Hunter Single Target Rotation[/color][/h3]
	[pad]
	Devourer in Single Target plays around a priority list, juggling both ability cooldowns and resources based on an order of power. This means with each GCD, we go top to bottom on a list, and press the button with the current highest value..[pad]
	[span display-options="void-scarred"] With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span][span display-options="annihilator"] With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span]


	[div display-options="!(void-scarred)&!(annihilator)"]
	[center][box border=true]
	[b][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-legendary-available] Please select a Hero Talent option to generate a Single Target priority[/b]
	[/box][/center]
	[/div]

[wrapper width=850px]
	[div display-options="void-scarred"]
	[wrapper][box border=true]
[center][b]Use the \u2716 markers to switch to common alternate talent picks based on your loadout.[/b]
[small][i]The build options used below are covered in the [url guide=32632]Talents page[/url]. Swaps not included should not change the priority in any meaningful way unless covered elsewhere. Anywhere you see the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.[/i][/small]
[/center] [/box] [/wrapper]


[pad]
[pad]

[b] Note: [spell=198793] is an [i]incredibly[/i] minor gain to use (0.3% ST, 1% aoe), if you are in a confined space, in danger if you use it, or just do not want to use it, then do not press it. It is not essential for the rotation, and is simply a free off gcd optimization.[/b]

	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=demon-hunter]Outside Void Metamorphosis Priority[/color][/h3]
[ol]
[li] Cast [spell=473662] if it will trigger [spell=1297432]. [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1226019] at 4+ souls. [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1241937] if one is not already active.  - [span class=tip tooltip=VSImmo][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1245412] if you are about to enter [spell=1217605]. - [span class=tip tooltip=VSBladeST][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li] Cast [spell=344866] after [spell=1245412] if about to enter [spell=1217605] and [spell=1246167] is available. - [span class=tip tooltip=Huggle][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li][/li] 
[li] Cast [spell=1246167] on cooldown. - [span class=tip tooltip=VSHuntST][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1217605] when available.[/li] 
[li] Cast [spell=1239519].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=198793] if buffed by [spell=1239526][/li]
[li] Cast [spell=473728].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=473662]. [/li]
[/ol]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=demon-hunter]Inside Void Metamorphosis Priority[/color][/h3]
[ol]
[li] Cast [spell=1217610] if it will trigger [spell=1297432].  [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1245453] at 4+ souls [b]or[/b] at maximum charges. [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1245470]. [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=198793] if buffed by [spell=1239526]. - [span class=tip tooltip=VSVr][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1245483].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1259431].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1245453] at 4+ souls.[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=473728].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1217610]. [/li]
[/ol]

		[center] [toggler id=void-scarred-ST hidden]Further Details [icon name=ui_profession_blacksmithing size=small type=round color=c12 inline=true][/icon][/toggler][/center]
		[div id=void-scarred-ST hidden]
		[symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color]'s single target rotation plays heavily around the talent [spell=1241532] and the start and end of your [spell=1217607] windows. Please see the sections below for further detail on the smuggling of melee abilities such as [spell=1246167] and [spell=1245412].

Unlike in the AoE rotation, we [b] DO NOT[/b] AFK to drop Meta, instead seeking to extend it as along as possible to fit in as many Culls as we can.

	[ol]
[li]Cast [spell=473662] if it will trigger [spell=1297432]. [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1226019] at 4+ souls. - [span class=tip tooltip=AnnVF][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]

[ol]

[li] Cast [spell=473728] unless it will overcap you on Souls  - [span class=tip tooltip=AnnSTVray][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1245453] at 4+ Souls [/li]
[li display-options="Annie-ST-Blade"] Cast [spell=1245412] - [span class=tip tooltip=VSMelee][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1221167] [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1217610] [/li]
[/ol]



	[/div]

[tab name="AoE Priority" icon=spell_holy_prayerofspirit]
	[h3 toc="AoE Priority" type=bar][color=c12] Best Devourer Demon Hunter AoE Rotation[/color][/h3]
	[pad]
In AoE, Devourer gains a lot of momentum due to the increased Soul Fragment generation provided by [spell=1227619]. We shift to a multi-target priority at [b]2 targets[/b], and both Hero Trees differ significantly on [i]where[/i] damage comes from, with [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] focusing more on [spell=1226033], and [symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color] focusing more on [spell=1221167].
	[span display-options="void-scarred"] In AOE, [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] does not follow a priority system inside of it's cooldowns, instead looking to execute an exact series of button presses, before dropping out of meta. As such, we've outlined the exact different phases and goals of each rotational phase below.[/span][span display-options="annihilator"] With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span]

	[div display-options="!(void-scarred)&!(annihilator)"]
	[center][box border=true]
	[b][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-legendary-available] Please select a Hero Talent option to generate a Single Target priority[/b]
	[/box][/center]
	[/div]

[wrapper width=850px]
	[div display-options="void-scarred"]
	[wrapper][box border=true]
[center][b]Use the \u2716 markers to switch to common alternate talent picks based on your loadout.[/b]
[small][i]The build options used below are covered in the [url guide=32632]Talents page[/url]. Swaps not included should not change the priority in any meaningful way unless covered elsewhere. Anywhere you see the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.[/i][/small]
[/center] [/box] [/wrapper]

[pad]
[pad]

[b] Note: [spell=198793] is an [i]incredibly[/i] minor gain to use (0.3% ST, 1% aoe), if you are in a confined space, in danger if you use it, or just do not want to use it, then do not press it. It is not essential for the rotation, and is simply a free off gcd optimization.[/b]

[symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color]'s AOE rotation can be broken down into 3 distinct phases, each with distinct goals. These phases, and their goals, are outlined below.

[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=demon-hunter]Inside Void Meta[/color][/minor-heading]

The majority of your damage occurs in this phase, and should be performed the exact same [b] every [/b] time. Our goal in this phase is to use all our melee abilities, cast [spell=1239524] and [spell=473728] twice, and leave the form with a proc of Eradicate (referred to as Shipping, which is outlined below). It is VERY important that you stop generating fury as soon as you have cast your second Void Ray, to drop out of Void Meta as quick as possible. 

[ol]
[li] Cast [spell=1239524] at 10 souls [b] if it is your first or second cast [/b] in this [spell=1217607] window. [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=473728] - [span class=tip tooltip=VSAoERay][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1217610] if it will trigger [spell=1297432] and you have not yet cast your second [spell=473728].  [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1245470]. [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=198793] if buffed by [spell=1239526]. - [span class=tip tooltip=VSVr][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1245483].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1259431].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1217610] if you have not yet cast your second [spell=473728]. [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=185123] if you have cast your second [spell=473728]. [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1241937] at 20 Fury or less remaining, before you drop out of [spell=1217607]. [/li]
[/ol]

An example Void Metamorphosis window would be as follows:

[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=473728]
[rt-step=1245412]
[rt-step=1217605]
[rt-half-step]
[rt-step=1236994]
[rt-step=1250533]
[/rt-half-step]
[rt-step=1239524]
[rt-step=473728 text="MUST be second global in Void Meta"]
[rt-step=1245470]
[rt-half-step]
[rt-step=198793]
[/rt-half-step]
[rt-step=1245483]
[rt-half-step]
[rt-step=1245470]
[rt-step=198793]
[/rt-half-step]
[rt-step=1259431]
[rt-half-step]
[rt-step=1245470]
[rt-step=198793]
[/rt-half-step]
[rt-step=1239524]
[rt-step=1217610 start loop-text="Repeat Untill Void Ray is Ready"]
[rt-step=1217610 end]
[rt-step=473728 text="Do not use Eradicate after this. Do Not generate Fury untill Void Meta Drops"]
[rt-step=185123 text="If AFK for longer than one global"]
[rt-step=1241937 text="Use at 20 Fury or less, as you drop out of Void Meta"]
[/rotation-timeline]

This rotation utilizes all your powerful abilities, before aiming to leave Void Meta as fast as possible with an Eradicate proc. This then flows into the next rotational phase.

[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=demon-hunter]Exiting Void Meta[/color][/minor-heading]

The first few globals after exiting [spell=1217605] are also important for maximizing your damage, due to the powerful buff from [spell=1244237]. Our goal here is to use the shipped [spell=1239524], get our cooldown of [spell=1241937] rolling, use [spell=473728], and to use any procs of [spell=1297432] which we may have. 

[ol]
[li] Cast [spell=473662] if it will trigger [spell=1297432]. [/li] 
[li] Cast [spell=1239524] at 10 souls. [/li]
[li] Cast [spell=473728].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1241937].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1246167] if off cooldown.[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=473662] if not at 10 Souls for [spell=1239524].[/li]
[/ol]

This will allow us to get the most damage into our [spell=1244237] window, while allowing us to setup for our next [spell=1217605]. An example of this window is as follows

[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=473662 text="If it will proc Soulburst"]
[rt-step=1239524]
[rt-step=473728]
[rt-step=1241937]
[rt-step=473662 text="until 10 Souls"]
[rt-step=1239524]
[/rotation-timeline]

[spell=1246167] should be used in this window if available, but it's CD does not always line up.


[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=demon-hunter]Rebuilding to Void Meta[/color][/minor-heading]

The final phase of [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color]'s AoE rotation returns to a more normal priorty list, wherein we try to generate as many souls as possible, and set up our next [spell=1217605] window. Our aim here is to return to Void Metamorphosis as quick as possible, and to smuggle (for more information on smuggling, please see the dedicated section down below) an [spell=1239524] and either [spell=1245412] or [spell=1246167] if available. It's important to note that we [b]ALWAYS[/b] want Eradicate, but only smuggle the melee abilities if they are off cooldown when Void Meta is ready, as we want to enter that form as fast as possible.

[ol]
[li] Cast [spell=473662] if it will trigger [spell=1297432]. [/li] 
[li] Cast [spell=1239524] at 10 souls if [spell=1217605] is [b]NOT[/b] ready.[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=473728].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1245412] if [spell=1217605] is ready.[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=344866] after [spell=1245412] if about to enter [spell=1217605] and [spell=1246167] is available. - [span class=tip tooltip=Huggle][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1246167] if available.  - [span class=tip tooltip=VSAoEHunt][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1217607].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1239519].[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=198793] if buffed by [spell=1239526].s[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=1241937] if one is not already active.[/li]
[li] Cast [spell=473662].[/li]
[/ol]

An example rotation would look as follows:

[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=1246167]
[rt-half-step]
[rt-step=1239519]
[rt-step=198793]
[/rt-half-step]
[rt-step=473662 start loop-text="Repeat until Void Ray is ready"]
[rt-step=1241937 text="if one is not active" end]
[rt-step=473728]
[rt-step=1239524]
[rt-step=473728]
[rt-step=1245412]
[rt-step=1217607]
[/rotation-timeline]








[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][color=demon-hunter]Putting it All Together[/color][/minor-heading]

[symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] cycles through three distinct rotational phases: [b]Meta Phase[/b] where most of our damage occurs and we execute a set combo of abilities, [b]Exit Meta Phase [/b] where we attempt to fit as many [spell=1239524] as possible into our [spell=1244237] buff, and our [b]Rebuild Phase[/b], where we try to return to [spell=1217605] as fast as possible, while smuggling in an Eradicate buff and a melee ability, when available. 

Each of these phases has a differing goal and rotational priority, and its recommended to learn each one as best as you can. To ease with learning this rotation, I've provided a short video of myself performing the rotation on the PTR target dummies, to showcase the general flow and the rotation in action.

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c12][icon name=Classicon_demonhunter_void_64 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c12][/icon] Devourer Demon Hunter Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]
Devourer is fairly straight forward in the number of Cooldowns it has access to on its spec tree. All of them come with some extra wrinkles in how they work rather than simply being flat increases, so the below section covers [i]how[/i] they work, and most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.

[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Void Metamorphosis" icon=inv_112_ability_demonhunter_metamorphasisvoid]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=demon-hunter] Void Metamorphosis\u200e [/color][/h3]
[spell=1217607] is your main damaging cooldown as a Devourer Demon Hunter, transforming you into a Void Empowered Demon form, and empowering your character in a variety of ways. 

Unlike most specializations, [spell=1217607] does not have a cooldown or a duration. Instead of a cooldown, it is available when you collect 50 Soul Fragments (or 35 Soul Fragments if you have the talent [spell=1247534]). Due to the talent [spell=1261684], we start combat with 25 Soul Fragments already collected, so a small period of ramp is needed before we have access to our cooldown. While inside of [spell=1217607], its duration is dependent on your Fury bar. Your Fury bar is instantly refilled when you enter and drains over time, ramping in drain intensity over time. Some of your abilities will briefly pause this drain, which we outline below.  

While in Void Metamorphosis, the following benefits apply:

[ul]
[li] Your Fury bar is refilled, and drains over time, increasing in drain speed the longer you are in Void Metamorphosis. Once your Fury bar reaches 0, you drop out of Void Metamorphosis.[/li]
[li] Your Mastery increases in power [/li]
[li][spell=473662] is upgraded into [spell=1217610], dealing more damage, having a shorter cast time, and reducing the cooldown of [spell=1226019] by 1 sec per cast[/li]
[li][spell=1226019] is upgraded into [spell=1245453], dealing more damage[/li]
[li][spell=473728] is upgraded, dealing more damage, costing no fury, and pausing your Fury drain while channeling it. It also gains a 14s hasted cooldown while inside of Void Metamorphosis. This cooldown does not persist outside of Void Metamorphosis [/li]
[li] You gain access to the powerful spell [spell=1221167] [/li]
[li] While inside of Void Metamorphosis, the following spells will briefly pause your fury drain:
     [ul]
     [li] [spell=473728] [/li]
     [li] [spell=1221167] [/li]
     [li] [spell=1245412] with the talent [spell=1272422] [/li]
     [li] [spell=1246167] with the talent [spell=1272422] [/li]
     [/ul]
[/li]
[li] [symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color] resets the cooldown of [spell=1226019], and automatically proc [spell=1256301].  [/li]
[li] [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] resets the cooldown [spell=1246167] and [spell=1245412]. Additionally, your abilities are further upgraded: 
      [ul]
           [li][spell=1245412] is upgraded into [spell=1245483][/li]
           [li][spell=1239519] is upgraded into [spell=1245470][/li]
           [li][spell=1246167] is upgraded into [spell=1259431][/li]
      [/ul]
    Furthermore, the first cast of each melee ability triggers a [spell=1246160] [/li]
[/ul]
[hr]
For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] you look to cycle through [spell=1217607] as fast as possible, leveraging the resets of powerful abilities and the high damage of [spell=1246160]. .

[symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color] instead looks to extend [spell=1217607], casting as many [spell=1221167] as possible. While it still likes to cycle through [spell=1217607] due to the free proc of [spell=1256301], it places a lot more value on being inside of [spell=1217607].
[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Collapsing Star" icon=inv_12_dh_void_ability_collapsingstar]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=demon-hunter] Collapsing Star [/color][/h3]

While not technically a cooldown in the traditional sense, [spell=1221167] is quite important for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color] at all target counts. [spell=1221167] is only accessible inside of [spell=1217607], and requires the collection of 30 Soul Fragments to be able to cast it. This spell deals a high amount of Single Target and AoE damage, and you should aim to cast as many as possible while inside of [spell=1217607]. 
[hr]

A tip to do this is known as Soul Smuggling. Soul Smuggling is the technique of leaving Soul Fragments on the ground when you go into or out of [spell=1217607]. By doing this, you are effectively "smuggling" those souls, allowing them to carry over and increase the speed to which you can reach your next [spell=1221167] or [spell=1217607]. 

[hr]

For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color], [spell=1221167] is especially important due to [spell=1253817] and [spell=1256307]. As [symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color], you should aim to cast at least 5 [spell=1221167] per [spell=1217607].

[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="The Melee Talents" icon=inv_12_dh_void_ability_reapersslice]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=demon-hunter] The Melee Talents[/color][/h3]

Unique for a caster specialization, Devourer Demon Hunter can choose a package of Melee Talents. These Melee talents form a package in the bottom left of your talent tree, and have special synergy with the [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] Hero Tree. The Melee Talents are as follows: 
[ul]
[li][spell=1245412][/li]
[li][spell=1239519][/li]
[li][spell=1272432][/li]
[li][spell=1272770][/li]
[li][spell=1247538][/li]
[li][spell=1272422][/li]
[li][spell=1240201][/li]
[li][spell=1246167][/li]
[/ul]
[hr]
When selected, these talents form what is known as the 'Melee Combo' for Devourer, which is as follows:
[ul]
[li] After dealing damage with [spell=1245412] or [spell=1246167], your Voidblade is replaced with [spell=1239519].[/li]
       [li] [spell=1239519] is an active, which deals Cosmic damage to enemies in 8 yards, generating 10 Fury and 2 Lesser Soul Shards. [/li]
       [li] After using [spell=1239519], you gain a free use of [spell=198793], and your next Vengeful Retreat within 6 seconds triggers [spell=1239526], dealing minor Cosmic damage to enemies within 8 yards.[/li]
[/ul]
This loop of abilities serves as a core, smaller cooldown loop for Hybrid builds of Devourer, but has extra synergy with the [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] tree. 
[hr]

With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color], the melee combo becomes a core part of the rotation, being buffed by multiple different talents. For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] the following bonuses apply to the melee combo:
[ul]
[li]While inside of [spell=1217607], your [spell=1245412] is upgraded into [spell=1245483], your [spell=1239519] is upgraded into [spell=1245470], and your [spell=1246167] is upgraded into [spell=1259431][/li]
[li] The first cast of each empowered ability triggers a powerful [spell=1246160][/li]
[li] Entering [spell=1217607] causes the cooldowns of [spell=1246167] and [spell=1245412] to reset with [spell=452409][/li]
[li][spell=452408] causes [spell=1245412] to deal additional damage as a DOT effect [/li]
[li][spell=452413] increases the critical strike damage and radius of [spell=1239519] [/li]
[/ul]

These effects lead to the melee abilities being essential for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color], as the Hero Tree does not work without them.
[pad]

For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color], the melee abilities form a core part of its gameplay, seeking to use them as often as possible to leverage their high damage. 

For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color] the melee abilities are predominantly used as a damage amp due to the powerful [spell=1241532] talent. Aim to use these abilities prior to casting [spell=1238488] buffed [spell=1245453] or [spell=1221167]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c12][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c12][/icon] Devourer Demon Hunter Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]
As a Devourer Demon Hunter, most of your high-level optimizations occur around getting to, and subsequently optimizing, your [spell=1217607] windows. These are where the majority of your damage comes from, and ensuring proper optimization of these is best for increasing your overall. Some advanced tips follow in the tabs below.

[pad]


[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Smuggling and Huggling" icon=inv_helmet_66]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c12] Smuggling [/color][/h3]
	If you've been around the Devourer Demon Hunter community for any length of time, you may have heard of an action called smuggling. While this is [b]NOT[/b] related to real life smuggling (this guide doesn't teach that, sorry), what it does describe is the action of taking a proc or resource into or out of [spell=1217607] where you otherwise wouldn't be able to. Generally speaking, Smuggling is often done with the following things:
[ul]
[li][spell=1227619][/li]
[li][spell=1239519][/li]
[li][spell=1226033] and [spell=1238488][/li]
[li] [spell=1246167][/li]
[/ul]
[pad]
Let's breakdown what Smuggling refers to in each of these cases, and [b]why[/b] you'd want to do it!
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c12]Shattered Souls[/color][/h3]

Soul Fragments serve as the most important resource for Devourer, powering you to access your key cooldown in [spell=1217607] while in normal form, or allowing you to cast the powerful [spell=1221167] when already inside of it. Soul Fragments for Devourer exist in two separate states, those collected outside of Void Metamorphosis, and those collected while already inside of it. Importantly, these stacks do not carry over when you change forms, and are wiped each time you enter or leave Void Metamorphosis. 

Thankfully, Soul Fragments do not automatically pick up, and we can have 10 lingering on the ground at any given time without collecting them. Because of these, we are able to leave Soul Fragments on the ground when we enter or leave Void Metamorphosis, and then collect them after. This allows us to enter Void Meta with more progress made towards Collapsing Star, or to leave Void Meta and have some progress made to get into our next one faster! 

[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c12]Hungering Slash[/color][/h3]
[pad]
By carrying any [spell=1239519] proc we have outside of [spell=1217607] into it, it upgrades into [spell=1245470], gaining 20% additional damage. On top of that, our damage further increases in Void Metamorphosis due to the second half of our mastery [spell=1238855], further increasing our damage. This allows us to get 3 supercharged [spell=1245470] per Void Metamorphosis, up from 2. 

While this is often done by utilizing [spell=1245412] prior to entering Void Metamorphosis, it can also be done with [spell=1246167]. This is often referred to as "Huggling" and has its own dedicated section down below. 

[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c12]Eradicate and Moment of Craving[/color][/h3]
[pad]
Similar to smuggling [spell=1239519], by smuggling [spell=1226033] and [spell=1238488] into [spell=1217607], we're able to take advantage of the 30% more damage that [spell=1245453] gains, as well as the additional damage we gain from our mastery [spell=1238855]. By smuggling [spell=1238488] into Void Meta, we're able to spend that on a Cull rather than a [spell=1226019]. Likewise, since [spell=473728] is reset upon entering Void Meta, we're able to use 2 Moment of Craving buffed Culls at the start of our burst, rather than 1. [spell=1226033] works similarly, upgrading into the "Cull" version when entering Meta, and doing 30% more damage (+damage from our mastery) as a result. While this behaviour is not currently used in Single Target, in AOE, we're aiming to smuggle an Eradicate into Void Meta [b]every[/b] time that we are able to. 

[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c12]Huggling[/color][/h3]

Newly discovered in S2 of Midnight, Huggling (Hunt Smuggling) is a turbo charged version of smuggling in a  [spell=1239519]. By pressing [spell=1217607] during the [b]travel time[/b] of The Hunt, we are able to activate our Meta Form [b]before[/b] The Hunt deals damage, upgrading it into [spell=1259431] prior to damage being dealt. This means we gain the upgraded damage on The Hunt, and are still able to smuggle in Hungering Slash. 

Performing this trick is fairly easy, requiring roughly 14% haste and enough distance so your gcd comes up during The Hunt travel. The easiest way to do this, and the way we recommend, is to [spell=1245412] followed by [spell=198793]. While midair from the Vengeful Retreat, cast The Hunt, and then press Void Metamorphosis as you travel towards your target. The animation will get locked out until you finish the charge, so it will look like nothing happened, but it *will* successfully Huggle. 

While ideally we want to always open a fight by huggling, we don't aim to do so every Void Metamorphosis, as The Hunt is a powerful spell which we don't want to lose uses of. Instead, after the opener, simply do this when this lines up. 


[/tab]
[tab name="Wiggling" icon=ability_seal]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c12]Wiggling[/color][/h3]
	Wiggling is another Devourer Demon Hunter specific behavior, due to one of our resources, Souls, existing on the ground. Wiggling refers to the behavior of moving slightly back and forth while casting, with the intention to pick up some soul fragments from the ground. While this is normally incorrect to do, as you will automatically collect any souls on the ground above 10, and we want [spell=1226019] to collect as many as possible due to [spell=1238739], there are situations where it's worthwhile to try and wiggle. Those are:
[ol]
[li] Less than 10 fury is needed to cast [spell=473728].[/li]
[li] Less than 4 souls are needed to cast [spell=1221167] and [spell=1226019] is on cooldown.[/li]
[li] You are very late into a [spell=471306] window, and collecting souls will allow you to cast another [spell=1221167].[/li]
[/ol]
In any of these situations, strafing left or right while casting [spell=473662] will allow you to pick up a few soul fragments, and greatly accelerate your rotation! 
[/tab]

[tab name="Shipping" icon=inv_10_engineering2_boxofbombs_friendly_color3]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c12]Shipping[/color][/h3]

Conversly to smuggling, which is the act of bringing things [b] into [/b] [spell=1217607], Shipping is where we bring things [b] out [/b] of Void Meta (since its legal get it). 

This is primarly done with 2 things, and only really done in [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] AoE 
[ul]
[li][spell=1217610] buffed with [spell=1297432].[/li]
[li][spell=1226033].[/li]
[/ul]

We aim to ship these out as they allow us to much quicker cycle through to our next Void Meta, rather than extend the tail end of our current one. Because of powerful passives like [spell=452414], [spell=452410], and [spell=1244237], our damage remains high outside of Void Meta. Thus, by shipping these spells out, they retain high damage, but also provide 10-20 souls towards our next Void Meta, allowing us to cycle through our cooldowns significantly faster than if we used them at the end of our previous one!


[/tab]
[tab name="Reap Usage" icon=inv_12_dh_void_ability_reap]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c12]Reap Usage[/color][/h3]

Following the changes to our season two tier set, [spell=1226019] has now mostly fallen out of the rotation for both Hero Trees, assuming you are facing 2 or more targets. It's use case varies depending on the target count and the selected Hero Tree, all of which are outlined below. 

[b]Single Target[/b]: In Single Target, Reap is used at 4+ souls for [b]BOTH[/b] Hero Talent trees, due to its strong damage.

[b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color] 2+ Targets[/b]: While fighting 2+ targets as [symbol=wow-hero-talent-void-scarred] [color=blue-gem]Void-Scarred[/color], Reap is essentially never used as it robs souls from [spell=1239524], making it harder to use this at 10+ Souls. While you can occasionally find places to weave a Reap in when you get lucky with procs, we generally do not recommend doing so as it will be a sizeable loss of AoE damage if you do starve Eradicate. If the priority damage is important, you can use Reap or Cull for more of it. 

[b][symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color] 2+ Targets[/b]: While fighting 2+ targets as [symbol=wow-hero-talent-annihilator] [color=whisper]Annihilator[/color], we go back to a season one rotational style, only using Reap if it will proc [spell=1256302], or give you enough souls to cast [spell=1221167]. Always aim to cast [spell=1239524] at 10 souls whenever possible. 

[/tab]

[/tabs]
[pad]

Our Devourer Demon Hunter guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Devourer Demon Hunter guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].


[tooltip name=VSImmo][color=q][spell=1272405] has a chance to reignite Soul Immo after a short delay. As such, always wait a gcd or two before reapplying it after one fades.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSSTReap][color=q] This is both a Fury generator and a high damage button. Try to use this when it will collect the max amount of souls, but make sure you're never overcapping on it's charges.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSMelee][color=q] This is used due to the Devouer's Bite talent. You want to only use this once per meta, right at the start to buff Voidsurge.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSSTVR][color=q] If you are in a dangerous spot and cannot move, you can forgo this ability.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=AnnSTVray][color=q]You can only have 40 Souls collected at once before wasting them, as such, if casting this will waste them, skip ahead to casting Collapsing Star.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSAoECStar][color=q]Collapsing Star is [b]VERY[/b] important for the caster variants of Void-Scarred, try to cast as many as possible for each Void Metamorphosis window! [/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSAoECStar][color=q]Collapsing Star is [b]VERY[/b] important for the caster variants of Void-Scarred, try to cast as many as possible for each Void Metamorphosis window! [/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSAoEMCstar][color=q]Collapsing Star is not very important for the Melee variants of Void-Scarred, only really taken to enable the Rolling Torment talent. If it is available and you are in a safe spot, you can use it, but don't go out of your way trying to do so. [/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSAoEVblade][color=q]As long as you don't lose any casts over the course of a dungeon, you should try and use Voidblade [i]right[/i] before you enter Void Metamorphosis, to upgrade your Hungering Slash into a Reaper's Toll.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSAOEReap][color=q]While Reap and Cull do no AoE damage, they are very strong priority damage for Void-Scarred. You should be looking to use them on cooldown when prio damage to a large mob matters, unless you are in very large (8-10+) pulls.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=AnnAOEErad][color=q]Try to always use this when it will consume 10 Soul Fragments.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSOpHS][color=q]You only use Hungering Slash [b]ONCE[/b] while inside of Void Metamorphosis. Allow the procs from Pierce the Veil and Predator's Wake to expire.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSAoEHS][color=q]In Cleave and AoE, use each charge of Reaper's Toll, not letting any expire.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=Smuggle][color=q]Always try to bring a proc of Eradicate into Void Meta![/color][/tooltip]


[tooltip name=SI][color=q]Soul Immolation is only used OUTSIDE of Void Meta! Don't use it while inside of Void Meta![/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSBladeST][color=q]Hold this button until Void Metamorphosis is ready. If Void Metamorphosis is ready and Voidblade is still on cooldown, skip smuggling and just enter Void Meta directly.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=Huggle][color=q]This Vengeful Retreat is only used if you are smuggling in The Hunt. Do not use it otherwise.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSHuntST][color=q]On pull, save The Hunt to smuggle into your first Void Meta. Outside of that, look to use The Hunt on cooldown, on smuggling it if it's off CD and you are about to enter Void Meta within a few GCDs.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSVr][color=q]Vengeful Retreat is a very minor damage gain for Void-Scarred, only worth about 0.3% of damage overall. As such, if you find yourself in a dangerous situation, you are free to skip these.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSAoEHunt][color=q]The Hunt is VERY powerful in AoE, and should be used on cooldown, not even saving off of pull to Hunt Smuggle. Hunt Smuggling is still a gain if it lines up naturally, but do not go out of your way to do this, as you want to cast The Hunt as many times as possible.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=VSAoERay][color=q]This [b]NEEDS[/b] to be your second global in Void Metamorphosis, otherwise your chance of getting to your second Void Ray cast lowers dramatically.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=AnnVF][color=q]Due to our Tier Set, we want to cast Reap every time it will consume 4 or more souls. As such, this will naturally spend your voidfall stacks, so do not worry too much about voidfall.[/color][/tooltip]
